question: How many double bonds are present in propanone?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Propanone, also known as acetone, has the chemical formula CH₃COCH₃.
 
• In its structure, propanone has a carbonyl group (C=O), which contains one double bond.
 
• The carbonyl group is positioned between two methyl groups (CH₃-), making it a ketone.
 
• Thus, propanone has only one double bond, which is the C=O bond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ketones:**

 
 
• Ketones are a class of organic compounds characterized by the presence of a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• Common examples include acetone (propanone) and butanone.
 
 
 
• **Carbonyl Group:**
 
 
• A carbonyl group is a functional group composed of a carbon atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom (C=O).
 
• It is a key feature in various organic compounds such as aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, and esters.
 
 
 
• **Propanone (Acetone):**
 
 
• Propanone is commonly used as a solvent in laboratories and in the manufacturing of plastics and other industrial products.
 
• It is also used in household items like nail polish remover.
 
 
 
• **Double Bond:**
 
 
• A double bond in chemistry refers to a chemical bond in which two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.
 
• Double bonds are stronger than single bonds and influence the shape and reactivity of molecules.
